prompt: recommend me some laptops between $800 and $1500 for coding
text:
# Laptop Recommendations for Coding ($800–$1500)

## Best Overall: Dell XPS 13 Plus (~$1,200–$1,400)
- 13.3" FHD or OLED display, Intel Core Ultra or AMD Ryzen
- Excellent build quality, light (~2.6 lbs), great keyboard
- Strong battery life (10–12 hours)
- Good thermal performance for sustained coding work

## Best Value: Lenovo ThinkPad E16 Gen 2 (~$900–$1,200)
- 16" IPS display (more screen real estate for split windows)
- AMD Ryzen 5 or 7, solid performance
- Durable, reputable keyboard
- Good upgrade path (RAM, storage accessible)

## Best for Performance: ASUS Vivobook Pro 16 (~$1,000–$1,400)
- 16" OLED display, AMD Ryzen 7
- Up to 32GB RAM and RTX 4060
- Great for multitasking or projects needing extra GPU
- Premium feel at mid-range price

## Budget Pick: Lenovo IdeaPad Flex 5 (~$800–$1,000)
- 14" or 16" touchscreen, AMD Ryzen 5
- 2-in-1 design (tablet mode if useful)
- Solid specs for the price
- Good portability

## MacBook Air M3 (~$1,100–$1,300)
- If you prefer macOS: exceptional battery, smooth performance
- Lightweight (~2.7 lbs), quiet
- Consider if your workflow is Mac-native

## Key specs to prioritize:
- **CPU**: Ryzen 5/7 or Intel Core Ultra/i5 minimum
- **RAM**: 16GB (32GB if heavy multitasking or Docker)
- **Storage**: 512GB SSD minimum
- **Display**: 14"–16" (larger helps with coding)
- **Battery**: 8+ hours real-world

Check current prices on Best Buy, Amazon, or Newegg—deals shift frequently. Return policy matters if you want to test keyboards and thermals.
